SOURCE livemint.com (UPI payment failed but money debited? Banks must ... - Mint): Millions of Indians hit “send” on UPI every day, only to watch their account get debited while the money never reaches the other side. When that happens, you are not expected to wait indefinitely or pay again. Under Reserve Bank of India (RBI) rules, banks must reverse the amount within fixed deadlines: T+1 day for person-to-person transfers and T+5 days for merchant payments, or automatically credit you ₹100 for every day the refund is delayed. A UPI transaction travels through several systems at once. The sender’s bank, the beneficiary’s bank, NPCI’s switching network, and the app itself. A glitch anywhere in this chain can leave the payment hanging even after your account is debited. The Reserve Bank’s framework on turnaround time and customer compensation for failed transactions sets clear deadlines. Under the RBI framework, a failed UPI person-to-person fund transfer, where the sender’s account is debited but the beneficiary’s account is not credited, must be automatically reversed within T+1 day if the credit cannot be completed. Here, T means the date of the transaction. For merchant payments where the account is debited but confirmation is not received at the merchant’s end, the prescribed auto-reversal timeline is T+5 days. If the bank misses the applicable deadline, compensation of ₹100 per day is prescribed for the delay. This compensation is credited automatically; you do not need to file a separate claim. Do not send the payment a second time until you confirm the status. Follow a documented escalation path instead. Open the UPI app and check whether the transaction is marked successful, failed, or pending. Save the reference number and confirm with the recipient. Raise a dispute inside the app using the help or transaction-specific option and note the complaint ticket number. NPCI’s UPI FAQs state that users can raise grievances or check transaction status through participating UPI apps. If the issue remains unresolved, lodge a formal complaint with the bank that holds your sending account. Share the transaction details and the app’s complaint reference, and ask the bank to trace the payment. You can also escalate through NPCI’s Register a Complaint portal, which routes the matter to the relevant institution. If the bank rejects the complaint, gives an unsatisfactory response, or does not reply within the set period, approach the RBI’s Complaint Management System under the Integrated Ombudsman framework. The RBI’s 2026 scheme came into effect on 1 July 2026. Keep every detail that helps the bank locate the payment. Retain the transaction reference number, date, amount, debit confirmation, recipient details, and complaint acknowledgement numbers. While you wait, stay alert. Scammers often exploit the urgency of a failed payment. Customers should not share their UPI PIN, OTP, passwords, or other authentication credentials. RBI के नियम के मुताबिक,अगर किसी व्यक्ति को पैसा किया है, तो पैसा न पहुंचने पर अगले दिन (T+1) तक अपने आप आपके खाते में वापस आ जाना चाहिए। वहीं दुकान या मर्चेंट को पेमेंट किया हो, तो 5 दिन (T+5) के अंदर पैसा वापस आना चाहिए। यहां T का मतलब है पेमेंट वाला दिन। अगर बैंक तय समय में पैसा वापस नहीं करता, तो उसे देरी के हर दिन के लिए 100 रुपये का हर्जाना देना होगा। इसके लिए आपको अलग से दावा नहीं करना पड़ता, यह पैसा अपने आप आपके खाते में आना चाहिए। पैसा न आए तो क्या करें? - UPI ऐप में देखें कि पेमेंट सफल, फेल या पेंडिंग है। ट्रांजैक्शन नंबर संभालकर रखें। - उसी पेमेंट पर जाकर हेल्प या डिस्प्यूट का ऑप्शन चुनें और शिकायत नंबर नोट कर लें। - बात न बने तो अपने बैंक में लिखित शिकायत करें। - NPCI की वेबसाइट पर शिकायत दर्ज करने का ऑप्शन है। - फिर भी हल न निकले, तो RBI के शिकायत पोर्टल पर शिकायत कर सकते हैं। ये चीजें संभालकर रखें ट्रांजैक्शन नंबर, तारीख, रकम, पैसा कटने का मैसेज, जिसे पैसा भेजा उसकी जानकारी और हर शिकायत का नंबर संभालकर रखें। इनसे आगे शिकायत करने और हर्जाना पाने में मदद मिलेगी। मैं, स्वाति, ET NOW स्वदेश में पिछले 9 महीनों से कॉपी एडिटर के रूप में जुड़ी हुई हूं। बिहार के दरभंगा की मूल निवासी और दिल्ली में पली-बढ़ी, मैंने अपनी शिक्षा दिल्ली विश्वविद्यालय के श्यामा प्रसाद मुखर्जी कॉलेज से पूरी की, जहाँ मैंने 2019 में हिंदी भाषा और साहित्य में स्नातक किया। इसके बाद, मैंने इग्नू से पोस्ट ग्रेजुएशन की डिग्री प्राप्त की। पत्रकारिता के प्रति मेरा रुझान कोविड-19 महामारी के दौरान बढ़ा, जिसने मुझे खबरों को पढ़ने, जानने और लिखने के लिए प्रेरित किया। इसके बाद बिना रुके 2021 से मैंने मीडिया जगत में अपना सफर शुरू किया, और अब मुझे इस क्षेत्र में कुल 4 साल का अनुभव है। अपने कार्यकाल के दौरान, मैंने मनोरंजन, लाइफस्टाइल, राजनीति, आध्यात्म, पर्सनल फाइनेंस और स्पोर्ट्स जैसी बीट्स पर काम किया है। जब मैं न्यूज़ रूम से बाहर होती हूँ, तो मुझे किताबें पढ़ना, यात्रा करना और नई चीजें सीखना पसंद है।... और देखें SOURCE news.abplive.com (UPI Payment Failed? RBI Says You Can Get Rs 100 Per Day For ...): UPI Payment Failed? RBI Says You Can Get Rs 100 Per Day For Delayed Refunds Money deducted but not received? RBI has a clear rule. If your UPI refund is late, banks must pay you ₹100 for every day of delay until your money is returned. - RBI mandates T+1 day refund for failed UPI transactions. - Banks must compensate Rs 100 daily for delayed refunds. - Raise disputes via UPI app; escalate to RBI CMS. Digital payments are part of daily life now. But when a UPI payment fails, and your money gets stuck, it becomes frustrating. You see “money deducted but not received” and don’t know what to do next. Most people just wait and hope the refund comes. What many users don’t know is that there is a clear rule for this. If your money is not returned on time, you are allowed compensation. RBI guidelines say banks must refund failed UPI transactions quickly. If they don’t, you are entitled to Rs 100 per day for the delay. UPI Failed Transaction Compensation Rule Explained The Reserve Bank of India has set a strict timeline for failed UPI payments. The refund must be completed within T+1 day. This means the day of the transaction plus one business day. If the refund does not arrive within this time, the bank is responsible for the delay. From the second day onward, you become eligible for UPI failed transaction compensation. The amount is Rs 100 for each day of delay until your money is returned. This rule exists to stop banks and apps from keeping user money pending for long periods. This applies only to cases where your account was debited, but the other person did not receive the money. It does not apply if you sent money to the wrong person or made a mistake while paying. Most users never claim this because they are not aware of it. They assume waiting is the only option. But the rule gives you a clear right. How To Claim UPI Failed Transaction Compensation First, wait until the T+1 day is over. Many refunds are processed within this time. If your money is still not back, open your UPI app and raise a dispute for that transaction. Every app has an option to report a failed payment. If the issue remains unresolved or you get no proper response, file a complaint on the RBI Complaint Management System at cms.rbi.org.in. Enter your transaction details and clearly mention that the refund has crossed the allowed time limit. State that you are claiming UPI failed transaction compensation as per RBI rules. RBI complaints are taken seriously by banks. In many cases, refunds are processed soon after this step. Some users also receive the extra amount for the days of delay. This process is simple. It protects your money and ensures delays are not ignored. You do not have to stay silent when your funds are stuck.
